notes: fix(refunds, semantic): the 'Refundable amount is 0 because overruleCode is null or CODE_DOES_NOT_EXIST' assertion was inverted. It encoded the assumption 'no overrule -> refund denied -> amount must be 0' as a global truth, but that's only correct in one specific case (booking outside every applicable afterSalesCondition window). The general truth is: WITHOUT overrule, the provider OWNS the rules (time/fare/distance/internal commercial — OSCAR can't predict them) and the response is authoritative; WITH overrule, the distributor declared the exceptional circumstance and the provider's contract is to refund the full booking value with no fee. Rewrote validateRefundableAmountLocal in `Bruno_Collection/library-bruno/refunds.js` to encode this correctly: (a) a new structural-bounds assertion that ALWAYS applies regardless of overrule (amount and fee non-negative; sum <= confirmedPrice; currencies consistent); (b) overrule-set branch verifies the overrule contract (full-refund: amount == confirmedPrice AND fee == 0; partial-with-overrule: fee == 0 AND fee+amount < confirmedPrice); (c) no-overrule branch logs what the provider returned but does NOT assert a specific value (OSCAR is not the source of truth for the provider's refund rules). The partial-refund identity (fee+amount < confirmedPrice strict) is preserved in both flows. Two consequences worth noting: a provider that ignored an overrule and returned a partial amount (historically silent pass) now fails; a no-overrule scenario whose booking is within the refund window (historically false positive failure) now passes with an [INFO] line surfacing the values for human reconciliation. The Paxone partial-refund scenario reported on 2026-06-09 — where no overrule was sent and Paxone returned 5000 EUR for a booking 9 days out — now correctly passes (was failing 'expected 5000 to equal 0').

fix(refunds, clarity): rename the partial-refund alignment assertion from 'Partial refund: response refundableAmount matches expected partial sum' to 'Partial refund: request/response alignment — response refundableAmount matches the sum of in-scope parts'. The historical wording sounded like a maths claim; the new wording names what is being verified (request vs response alignment). The error message already includes the wire-scope shape (e.g. `fulfillment[b90ddfa8...].bookingParts (6 part(s))`) so a failure is self-explanatory.

fix(refunds, clarity): provider timestamps come back in UTC (e.g. createdOn=2026-06-09T05:23:26+00:00); the assertion messages now append a parenthetical Europe/Paris equivalent so the report shows both the UTC string and the local-time read at once (e.g. '... is valid and in the past: 2026-06-09T05:23:26+00:00 (= 2026-06-09 07:23:26 Europe/Paris)'). No assertion-logic change; pure display improvement that prevents the tester from mentally doing the +1h/+2h offset against their local clock.

feat(#218 follow-up, golden rule): the Test Framework now gates scenario features. A scenario may not silently exercise a capability the framework hasn't declared — 'what is not defined in the framework cannot be tested'. Implemented as SOFT validation (option (a)-with-scan): existing scenarios keep working, runs are never blocked, but warnings are surfaced at three levels so the gap is visible. First feature gated: partial refund (partialRefundByLeg / partialRefundByPax → REFUND_PARTIAL in salesFlows[]). New `Oscar_Server/src/utils/frameworkGating.js` is the single source of truth for the field↔flow rule table (`gatingRules()`), the per-scenario warning resolver (`scenarioWarnings()`), the lazy server-side migration (`applyFrameworkMigration()`), and the datafile annotator (`annotateDatafile()`). Three integration points: (1) `GET /v1/company/test-framework` now runs a one-time lazy migration per framework — when the framework's salesFlows[] doesn't include REFUND_PARTIAL but at least one of the company's scenarios arms partialRefundByLeg/byPax, REFUND_PARTIAL is added to salesFlows[], a `_salesFlowsMigratedAt` audit stamp is written, and the row is re-encrypted. Conservative: adds only, never removes — so a Test Manager's running configuration is preserved exactly while the new declaration baseline reflects what they're actually using. (2) `GET /v1/company/datafile` now annotates each scenario whose armed feature isn't declared with `__featureNotDeclaredWarnings: [field, ...]` before serving — on-disk file is unchanged; only the served bytes carry the annotation. (3) `Bruno_Collection/library-bruno/scenarioParser.js` reads the annotation and emits a `[WARNING]` log line per entry at scenario load, explaining which capability isn't declared and how to silence the warning. Wizard UI (`Oscar_Server/public/js/scenarios.js`): an inline amber chip next to the partial-refund block when the scenario arms it without the framework declaring it, plus a top-of-scenarios banner with the count of affected scenarios and a pointer to Test Framework → ✂️ Refund/Exchange row. Both check `fwDeclaresPartialRefund(scenarioType)` against the framework's salesFlows[]. New `tests/unit/framework-gating.test.js` covers 26 cases including the integration scenario: pre-migration warnings → migration runs → re-annotation finds nothing to warn about. No data-file schema change, no backend behaviour change beyond the warnings.

fix(#218, partial refund): alignment assertion now compares against the actual wire scope, not the resolver's internal intent. Follow-up to v1.11.103: a Paxone test against a 4-pax / 2-leg booking with both axes armed (per-leg=last + per-pax=last) sent the correct fulfillmentIds=['<nicolas's fulfillment>'] (single, scoped, OSDM-3.5 compatible) and Paxone correctly refunded all 6 of nicolas's parts across both legs (refundableAmount=5000 EUR = sum of the fulfillment.bookingParts). The new alignment assertion however computed expected=2500 (the resolver's per-leg-x-per-pax intersection of 3 parts on the last leg only) and cried wolf — because on OSDM v3.5 the per-leg axis is silently dropped at the wire (refundSpecifications.bookingPartIds is not yet supported). The expected sum now depends on what was actually conveyed: refundSpecifications.bookingPartIds when on the wire (provider refunds exactly those), refundSpecifications.passengerIds-only when on the wire (provider expands to every part owned by those passengers), or fulfillment.bookingParts[].id when only fulfillmentIds[] is on the wire (provider refunds everything in the scoped fulfillment). Plus a new [WARNING] log line when an axis is silently dropped due to osdmVersion < 3.8 — explains in plain English that the per-leg request couldn't be conveyed and the response will cover all legs of the chosen passenger. The error message now also names the wire-scope shape so the failure is self-explanatory.

fix(#218, partial refund): the wizard-generated request was malformed in five distinct ways and the response was treated as a partial refund even when the provider had silently produced a full one. Discovered debugging a Paxone REFUND scenario where the response refundableAmount equalled the booking's full confirmedPrice — i.e. partial scope was never actually applied. Five fixes: (1) `Bruno_Collection/library-bruno/bookings.js` was pushing every fulfillment id TWICE into the env var, so refund / exchange requests carried each id duplicated — providers tolerated it for full-flow but partial scope couldn't work. Dedupe to one push per fulfillment. (2) `library-bruno/requestsBuilder.js` now trims `fulfillmentIds[]` to the scoped fulfillment when partial is armed; the original code kept the full list AND added refundSpecifications, which providers correctly interpreted as 'refund all these in full'. (3) `library-bruno/partialRefund.js` now resolves `RefundSpecification.fulfillmentId` by matching `fulfillment.fulfillmentParts[].passengerRef` against the chosen passenger's externalRef — the old code blindly picked fulfillments[0], which is wrong on providers like Paxone that model one-fulfillment-per-passenger. (4) Leg ordering now reads `booking.trips[*].legs[*].id` (the user-visible leg list the wizard's first/last/outbound/inbound labels refer to), instead of treating the legs × passengers cross-product of admissions as the leg list. (5) Booking-part expansion now walks `admission.reservationRefs[].id` and `admission.ancillaryRefs[].id` instead of looking for `requiredAdmissionKey | admissionRef | admissionId` on the reservation/ancillary side — those fields don't exist in OSDM / Paxone. The two axes also now intersect explicitly (admissions covering the chosen leg AND owned by the chosen passenger), so leg-target and pax-target never disagree on the subject. Plus: when the negotiated `osdmVersion < 3.8` (e.g. Paxone sandbox on 3.5), `refundSpecifications[]` is omitted (the provider would reject it as OSDM_EXTRA_REQUEST_FIELDS_IGNORED and silently full-refund); scoping then happens via the trimmed `fulfillmentIds[]` alone. New after-response alignment assertion compares `response.refundOffers[0].refundableAmount` against the sum of the in-scope booking-part prices computed before the request and fails with a clear message if the provider ignored the scope — the symptom that started this investigation now surfaces as a test failure instead of a silent full refund. Resolver covered by a 4-case smoke trace against a Paxone-shaped fixture (deleted before commit).

fix(#204): the per-scenario expiredBookingMaxWaitMinutes timer (shipped in 2026.116) silently did not extend the worker SIGTERM because computeEffectiveRunTimeoutMs in runner.js read the datafile with plain fs.readFile + JSON.parse — but since OSCAR v1.11.0 (Phase 2 of issue #60) the datafile on disk is AES-256-GCM encrypted under the OSCAR1 envelope. JSON.parse(ciphertext) threw, the catch block silently swallowed the error, and the helper fell back to base RUN_TIMEOUT_MS — so every scenario opting into Max wait got SIGTERMed at 10 min regardless. Tester report: set Max wait=30 on Paxone (deadline ~15 min) → run died at exactly 10m with exit 1 and no transaction reports. Fix: helper now uses decryptFromFileAsync (same pattern as the /v1/runs POST handler in api/routes/runs.js), which handles both encrypted and legacy plaintext datafiles. Also: the runner now ALWAYS logs the effective RUN_TIMEOUT_MS chosen for the run (with base / requested / hardMax / source / helperError fields) — previously the diagnostic only fired when the extension actually fired, which is exactly when this kind of failure can't be diagnosed. New Jest test tests/unit/runner-effective-timeout.test.js pins the contract: encrypted+plaintext datafiles, sanity (off), clamping at RUN_HARD_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, helper-error reporting, scenariosToRun=ALL, all four expiredBookingTest truthy forms. Server-only release; no Bruno collection bump. Server 1.11.89 -> 1.11.90.

fix(critical): v19 migration crash on boot, leaving OSCAR in restart-loop. Migration used SELECT rowid + UPDATE WHERE rowid = ?, but Node 22's built-in node:sqlite does not expose rowid as a row property — r.rowid was undefined and binding failed with 'Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 2'. Switched to the explicit `id` primary key (uniform across all four affected tables). Also added per-row error isolation so a single unbindable row doesn't abort the whole table's migration.

The v19 migration backfill is idempotent and can be skipped on small instances if desired.
